zh.title: 模型怎样利用图像推理：一起生成、反复看图与按需读取
zh.summary: 画出的路线和写出的步骤，为什么会各自正确却互相矛盾？今天主读 10 月 20 日的 JUICE，理解图像与文字怎样共同生成。选读 CVRR，看怎样检验答案真正依赖视觉隐状态；再读 ViMoD，看长推理中如何按需读取图像细节。三篇均为近期预印本，分别回答生成如何协调、内部计算是否必要、视觉证据如何访问。先读主读的迷宫例子，选读按兴趣展开。

en.title: How Models Use Images to Reason: Joint Generation, Re-reading, and Selective Access
en.summary: Why can a drawn route and written moves each be correct yet contradict one another? The main reading, JUICE from October 20, explains how image and text can be generated together. CVRR examines whether answers really depend on visual latent states; ViMoD studies selective access to image details during long reasoning. These recent preprints address coordinated generation, necessary internal computation, and access to visual evidence. Start with the main reading’s maze example and explore the companions as interest permits.

papers.title: JUICE: Unified Multimodal Modeling in Pretrained Representation Spaces
papers.venue: arXiv 2026 · NYU / Harvard / UIUC / Princeton / UPenn · v1 2026-10-20

zh.contribution: 在冻结的图像和文字表征空间中，用同一流匹配主干生成两种内容；每轮共同更新，让尚未完成的图文相互参考。
zh.relevance: 补齐多模态生成与视觉推理的建模视角，也帮助辨别主干参数、完整流水线成本和缓存可复用条件。
zh.prerequisites: 向量表征、attention、从噪声逐步生成；正文先给直观解释，不要求先熟悉流匹配数学。
zh.caveat: 迷宫需要额外训练，联合采样未超过最好的顺序基线；通用知识和长文字仍弱，2.1B 不含全部冻结组件。

sections.heading: 先看一个问题：图和文字都答对了，为什么还算失败？
paragraphs: 假设一张迷宫有两条最短路线。模型画出了沿上方绕行的蓝线，却在文字里写了沿下方绕行的步骤。单独检查图或文字，都能走到终点；把两者作为同一个答案交给用户，就对不上了。这是 JUICE 最适合入手的例子：它研究怎样同时生成图像和文字，让两者在生成过程中保持联系。
这是一篇 2026 年 10 月 20 日的预印本，来自 NYU、Harvard、UIUC、Princeton、UPenn 的研究者。推荐它主要是因为建模方式和对照实验有启发性：不仅把两种输出放进同一模型，还允许尚未完成的图像和文字共同变化。它没有证明通用视觉推理已经解决，也没有把这种过程当作自然语言思维链的替代品。

sections.heading: 第一步：把图像和文字都变成可以连续修改的向量
paragraphs: 通常，文字生成是在词表里一个 token 接一个 token 地选；图像生成则可以从噪声开始，反复修改整张图的连续状态。JUICE 先把两种输入都交给预训练编码器。编码器把内容转换成一组向量，这些向量叫表征；比如图像中的局部形状、文字在上下文中的含义，都可以影响向量的数值。
默认方案用 SigLIP2 编码图像，用 Flan-T5-Small 编码文字。图像得到 256 个位置的表征，文字使用 128 个位置。这里是分别进入各自的连续空间，经过投影后再交互，并不是说图像向量天然等于文字向量。编码器在主干训练中保持冻结，所以它们已经学过的知识仍然是模型能力的来源。
新训练的 Transformer 叫 MM-RiT，负责在这些空间里预测图像和文字的状态。最后，图像解码器把状态还原成像素，文字解码器把状态读成 token。因此，“没有预训练语言模型初始化”特指 MM-RiT 主干；整个系统仍然利用预训练编码器，以及分别训练后在主干训练中固定的解码器，不能理解为所有能力都从零学起。

sections.heading: 第二步：用两个进度值，说明哪些内容已知、哪些还要生成
paragraphs: 论文用 t 表示从噪声走向完整数据的进度：t=0 是纯噪声，t=1 是干净的表征。训练时把一份噪声 ε 和真实表征 z 混合，得到 z(t)=(1−t)ε+t·z。网络看到混合后的状态，学习预测干净的 z。Flow matching（流匹配）可以先理解为：学会一个更新方向，让噪声经过多步更新，最终变成像训练数据那样的表征。
JUICE 为图像和文字各设一个进度值。给定一句话画图时，文字保持 t=1，图像从 0 走向 1；看图写描述时则反过来；同时生成图文时，两边都从噪声出发。视觉问答还可以细到每个位置：输入图片和问题保持不变，只更新回答部分。
这解释了论文图 2 中的正方形：横轴和纵轴分别表示两种进度，沿边走对应一种内容已知，穿过内部对应两边都在生成。两个进度可以采用不同的变化节奏，并不要求图和文字以完全相同的速度成形。

sections.heading: 第三步：每一轮都让两边看到对方的当前状态
paragraphs: MM-RiT 内部先分别为图像和文字计算 Q、K、V，再把两组序列放进同一次双向 attention。Attention 可以理解为根据当前内容，从其他位置取回有关信息；双向意味着图像位置能参考文字位置，文字位置也能参考图像位置。两种内容仍保留各自的投影和前馈网络。
联合采样时，模型先基于同一份“当前图像状态＋当前文字状态”算出两边的更新方向，然后再更新两边。下一轮看到的就是两份都已推进的状态。论文称其为 coupled sampling。它不是先把整段文字写完，再要求图像照着画，也不是两条互不通信的生成流程。
需要注意，过程里相互影响的是连续向量，不是模型在每轮都说出一段可读的解释。论文把中间状态解码后展示出来，是为了观察生成过程；不能据此认定每次更新都对应人能命名的推理步骤。

sections.heading: 训练为什么不能只做“看图说话”和“按话画图”
paragraphs: 如果训练时总是一边完全正确、另一边等待生成，模型就很少见到“两边都还没完成”的情况。联合生成恰好一直经过这种状态。默认预训练因此混合三类样本：55.6% 同时对图文去噪，22.2% 给文字生成图，22.2% 给图生成文字。网络只对当前需要生成的部分计算去噪损失。
反过来，只训练两边都有噪声也不够。真正做问答或文生图时，条件端是完整输入，而不是带噪声的近似。作者同时训练两类状态，目的是让训练覆盖推理实际经过的情况。这个思路很值得记住：任务看起来都叫“生成图文”，执行时的信息条件却可能不同。
GenEval 检查生成图是否满足对象、数量、颜色和相对位置等要求。在 668M 主干的配方对照里，混合训练的 GenEval 为 48.41%，只做两个条件方向为 36.30%，只做联合去噪为 31.33%。数据、主干和训练计划保持一致；作者还增加监督目标数量匹配、阻断图文交互等对照。混合方案的优势不完全能由“多监督了一些目标”解释。但每个配置只训练一次，不能把这一比例当成所有规模的最佳配方。

sections.heading: 回到迷宫：两份答案怎样逐步选择同一条路线
paragraphs: 把输入迷宫和问题固定，给“画出路线的目标图”和“移动步骤的目标文字”各自一份噪声。第一次更新后，两边还可能含有多种路线的信息；后续更新时，每一边都能利用另一边当前的状态。论文展示的两个样例中，一个是文字较早稳定、图像随后改到相同路线，另一个是图像先稳定、文字随后跟上。
这是对中间状态的观察，不是人为写入了“谁先决定就听谁的”规则。也不能仅凭两个样例断言模型学到了通用规划算法。它支持的较窄结论是：在这些任务上，两条生成流确实可以在不同方向上相互协调，而不必预先固定生成顺序。

sections.heading: 最关键的实验：公平比较的是主干调用次数
paragraphs: 多解迷宫实验使用 2.1B 主干，并在相关任务上额外适配 5,000 次更新。训练集有 20 万个例子，尺寸为 5×5、6×6、7×7；测试是 500 个未在训练中出现的布局，每个迷宫有 2–16 条最短路线。评分要求图和文字都给出合法最短路径，而且必须是同一条；不是要求复现唯一的参考答案。
表 7 比较相同的 16 次主干调用、两个采样种子的平均结果。SigLIP2 版本独立生成的联合成功率是 54.6%，联合采样为 93.7%，先文字后图为 85.3%，先图后文字为 95.2%。因此，联合采样解决了大量不一致问题，但没有超过最好的顺序基线；附录 D.2 对 SigLIP2 的配对检验也发现先图后文字更好。
预算细节不能漏：联合采样一次调用同时更新两边，所以是 16 个共享步骤；独立或顺序方案各给两边 8 步。这里不计编码器、解码器调用，也不是相同端到端耗时的证明。图 11 的展示样例又给独立方案两边各 16 步，共 32 次调用；看图时不能把它和表 7 的预算混为一谈。

sections.heading: 一般图文任务上有哪些收益，又付出了什么代价？
paragraphs: 最终两种 2.1B 模型都生成 224×224 图像。文生图使用 25 个 Euler 更新步骤、guidance=5；GenEval 上 DINO 版本为 0.88，SigLIP2 版本为 0.87。视觉问答使用 16 步、guidance=3；SigLIP2 在 VQAv2 test-dev 得到 73.1。Euler 是逐步推进状态的数值方法；guidance 用条件预测与参考预测的差异，增强条件对结果的影响。
这些分数并不表示全面领先。表 6 中 SigLIP2 版本在 AI2D 图解题上是 34.4，MMMU 是 29.6，弱于若干从预训练语言模型开始的对照。长描述还会出现语法问题或臆造词。668M 控制实验里，连续文字方案的图文语义匹配 CLIPScore 接近自回归方案，但与参考措辞重合的 CIDEr 明显较低。语义相关和文字表达可靠性需要分别评价。
同样要谨慎理解“多一种能力不损伤画图”。共同 guidance 下，JUICE 的 GenEval 48.41% 接近文生图专用模型的 47.86%；分别调整 guidance 后，专用模型达到 51.23%，超过 JUICE。论文支持特定配方下的取舍分析，并没有证明统一模型永远没有代价。

sections.heading: 从系统角度读：2.1B 不是全部成本
paragraphs: 附录 A.5 明确区分可训练主干和完整流水线。较大 SigLIP2 方案的主干约 2.12B；把双向任务需要的编码器和解码器都加载后，合计约 3.03B。它们虽然被冻结，推理时仍然可能需要计算和显存。因此，比较部署成本时不能只看摘要中的 2.1B。
正文定量问答使用并行文字解码器，一次读取所有回答位置；迷宫则使用单独训练的线性任务头。部分图文联合生成的展示图用的是自回归文字解码器。这些路径应分开理解，不宜说所有结果都通过同一个“全并行文字出口”得到。
下面是我的系统推论：当两边状态每一轮都变化、attention 又是双向的，不能直接套用自回归模型“已生成前缀永远不变”的 KV 复用假设。实际实现还需要逐层检查哪些条件计算可缓存。论文的主干调用预算也不能自动换算成 serving 吞吐或延迟；本篇不把它包装成已验证的推理加速方案。

sections.heading: 怎么读最划算
paragraphs: 值得精读。先用 10 分钟看图 1、图 2 和表 7，抓住“两个生成进度＋两边一起更新”；再读 §3.2–3.5，最后看 §4.3 的训练对照和附录 D.1–D.2 的评分与预算。如果还想了解文本为什么能连续生成，再读 A.4 的解码器。
先修只需要三件事：向量表征是内容的一种编码；attention 让一个位置读取其他位置；噪声生成通过多次更新逐渐形成输出。暂时不必先掌握流匹配的全部数学。读完应能回答：联合生成和独立生成究竟差在哪一步，为什么训练需要覆盖两边都不完整的状态，以及为什么 93.7% 不是“通用视觉推理成功率”。

sections.heading: 原始资料与版本
paragraphs: 核验版本：[JUICE，arXiv:2610.28801v1，2026-10-20](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.28801v1)。本文是依据 Jiahan Li 等人的论文撰写的解释与评议；原论文采用 [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) 许可。实验数字取自该固定版本，例子和系统推论已在文中区分。未核到正式会议录用信息，因此标作预印本。

en.contribution: One flow-matching backbone generates frozen image and text representations, updating both streams together so unfinished outputs can condition one another.
en.relevance: Builds intuition for multimodal generation and visual reasoning, while separating backbone size, full pipeline cost, and conditions for cache reuse.
en.reading: Worth close reading: Figures 1–2 and Table 7, then Sections 3.2–3.5 and 4.3 and Appendices D.1–D.2.
en.prerequisites: Vector representations, attention, and iterative generation from noise; the note introduces the intuition before flow-matching mathematics.
en.caveat: Mazes require task adaptation; coupling does not beat the best sequential order. Knowledge and long text remain weak, and 2.1B excludes frozen components.

sections.heading: A puzzle: both answers are valid, so why does the pair fail?
paragraphs: Imagine a maze with two shortest routes. A model draws a blue path around the upper side but writes moves around the lower side. Either output reaches the goal, yet they do not describe the same solution. This is an accessible entry point to JUICE: it studies how image and text can be generated together while influencing one another along the way.

This October 20, 2026 preprint is by researchers at NYU, Harvard, UIUC, Princeton, and UPenn. Its value lies in the modeling choice and controlled experiments: unfinished image and text states can evolve together. It does not establish general visual reasoning or show that this process replaces natural-language chain of thought.

sections.heading: Step 1: represent both modalities as continuously editable vectors
paragraphs: Text is commonly generated by choosing vocabulary tokens one at a time, while image generation can repeatedly revise a continuous state starting from noise. JUICE first passes both modalities through pretrained encoders. These produce representations: vectors whose values carry information about image regions or words in context.

The default uses SigLIP2 for images and Flan-T5-Small for text, yielding 256 image positions and 128 text positions. They inhabit separate continuous spaces and are projected before interacting; an image vector is not inherently a text vector. The encoders remain frozen during backbone training, so their pretrained knowledge is an important source of capability.

A newly trained Transformer, MM-RiT, predicts states in these spaces. Fixed decoders subsequently turn them into pixels and tokens. “No language-model initialization” refers to the MM-RiT backbone, not to an entire system without pretrained components.

sections.heading: Step 2: use two progress values to specify what is given
paragraphs: The paper uses t for progress from noise to clean data: t=0 is pure noise and t=1 is a clean representation. During training, noise ε and a true representation z are mixed as z(t)=(1−t)ε+t·z. The network learns to predict clean z from this mixture. An intuitive view of flow matching is learning update directions that move noise toward a data-like representation over multiple steps.

JUICE assigns separate progress values to image and text. For text-to-image generation, text stays at t=1 while the image advances from 0 to 1; captioning reverses the roles. Joint generation starts both from noise. Visual question answering specifies this per position: the image and question stay fixed while answer positions are generated.

This explains the square in Figure 2. Its axes are the two progress values. Paths along an edge have one clean modality; paths through the interior generate both. Their schedules can differ, so the modalities need not become clear at the same rate.

sections.heading: Step 3: each update uses both current states
paragraphs: Within MM-RiT, image and text first have separate Q, K, and V projections. Their sequences then participate in one bidirectional joint attention operation. Attention retrieves relevant information from other positions; bidirectionality lets image positions use text positions and vice versa. Each modality retains its own output projections and feedforward networks.

During coupled sampling, the model computes both update directions from the same current image–text state before updating either stream. The next step therefore sees both advanced states. This differs from completing the text before drawing, and from two independent generation processes.

The interacting objects are continuous vectors, not readable explanations emitted at every step. Decoding intermediate states helps inspect the process; it does not show that every update corresponds to a human-interpretable reasoning operation.

sections.heading: Why conditional tasks alone are insufficient training
paragraphs: Training only with one complete modality and one generation target rarely exposes the model to two unfinished modalities. Joint generation repeatedly encounters exactly that condition. Default pretraining mixes 55.6% joint denoising, 22.2% text-to-image, and 22.2% image-to-text examples. Denoising loss applies to the current generation targets.

Training only on jointly noisy inputs is also insufficient: actual question answering and text-to-image inference have exactly clean conditions. Mixing these tasks covers the information conditions encountered during inference. Tasks that all sound like “generate image and text” can expose the network to substantially different states.

GenEval checks whether generated images satisfy requirements such as objects, counts, colors, and relative positions. At 668M backbone size, the mixed recipe obtains 48.41% GenEval, versus 36.30% for the two conditional directions alone and 31.33% for joint denoising alone. Data, backbone, and training schedule are shared. Further controls match supervised target counts or block cross-modal exchange, showing that additional targets do not fully explain the improvement. Each configuration is trained once, however, and the mixture is not established as optimal across scales.

sections.heading: Back to the maze: converging on the same route
paragraphs: Keep the input maze and question fixed, and initialize the target solved image and target move sequence with noise. Early states may still accommodate multiple routes. Subsequent updates allow each stream to use the other’s evolving state. In two illustrated cases, the moves stabilize first and the image follows, or the image stabilizes first and the moves follow.

These are observations of intermediate states, not an explicit rule that the first stream to decide becomes authoritative. Two examples also do not prove a general planning algorithm. The narrower supported conclusion is that coordination can occur in either direction on these tasks without a predefined generation order.

sections.heading: The decisive comparison matches backbone calls
paragraphs: The multiple-solution maze experiment adapts the 2.1B models for another 5,000 updates. Training uses 200,000 examples at 5×5, 6×6, and 7×7 grid sizes. Evaluation uses 500 unseen layouts, each with 2–16 shortest routes. Joint success requires two legal shortest routes that are the same route, rather than matching a unique stored reference.

Table 7 compares 16 backbone calls and averages two sampling seeds. For SigLIP2, independent sampling achieves 54.6% joint success, coupled sampling 93.7%, text-first sampling 85.3%, and image-first sampling 95.2%. Coupling removes many disagreements but does not outperform the best sequential baseline. Appendix D.2 also finds image-first significantly better than coupling for SigLIP2 in its paired test.

A coupled call updates both streams, giving 16 shared steps. Independent and sequential methods receive eight steps per stream. Encoder and decoder calls are excluded, so this does not establish equal end-to-end latency. Figure 11 uses a different illustrative budget: independent sampling gets 16 steps per stream, or 32 calls. Its pictures should not be read as the exact budget comparison in Table 7.

sections.heading: What improves on general tasks, and what remains weak?
paragraphs: The final 2.1B variants generate 224×224 images. Text-to-image uses 25 Euler updates with guidance=5; DINO reaches 0.88 GenEval and SigLIP2 0.87. Visual question answering uses 16 steps with guidance=3; SigLIP2 reaches 73.1 on VQAv2 test-dev. Euler integration advances the state step by step. Guidance strengthens the condition’s effect using the difference between conditioned and reference predictions.

These scores do not imply broad superiority. The SigLIP2 variant scores 34.4 on AI2D and 29.6 on MMMU in Table 6, below several models initialized from pretrained language models. Longer descriptions can contain grammatical errors or invented words. In the 668M control, continuous text nearly matches autoregressive text on semantic image–caption CLIPScore but scores much lower on CIDEr, which measures agreement with reference phrasing. Semantic relevance and reliable wording deserve separate evaluation.

The claim that adding another ability preserves image generation is also conditional. At shared guidance, JUICE obtains 48.41% GenEval versus 47.86% for the text-to-image-only reference. With guidance tuned separately, that specialized model reaches 51.23%, exceeding JUICE. This is evidence about a particular design tradeoff, not a general guarantee that unification is free.

sections.heading: A systems reading: 2.1B does not count the entire pipeline
paragraphs: Appendix A.5 distinguishes trainable backbone size from the complete pipeline. The large SigLIP2 backbone is about 2.12B parameters; loading the components needed for both directions brings the total to approximately 3.03B. Frozen components can still consume inference compute and memory, so deployment comparisons should not use only the abstract’s backbone count.

Quantitative question answering uses a parallel text decoder that reads all answer positions at once. Mazes use a separately trained linear task head. Some qualitative joint image–text samples use an autoregressive text decoder. These paths should remain distinct; not every displayed result uses the same fully parallel text readout.

The following is my systems inference: when both streams change each round and attention is bidirectional, autoregressive KV reuse assumptions based on an immutable generated prefix do not transfer directly. Actual implementations would need to identify reusable condition computations layer by layer. Backbone-call budgets also do not translate automatically into serving throughput or latency; this note does not present JUICE as a demonstrated inference speedup.

sections.heading: How to read it efficiently
paragraphs: Worth a close read. Start with Figures 1–2 and Table 7 to understand two progress values and coordinated updates. Then read Sections 3.2–3.5, the training controls in Section 4.3, and scoring and budgets in Appendices D.1–D.2. Read Appendix A.4 afterward if continuous text generation and readout interest you.

Only three starting concepts are essential: representations encode content as vectors; attention lets positions retrieve information from other positions; noise-based generation forms outputs through repeated updates. The full mathematics of flow matching can wait. The useful questions are exactly where coupled and independent generation differ, why training must include two unfinished modalities, and why 93.7% is not a general visual-reasoning success rate.

papers.title: Reason Through the Latent! Making Latent Visual Reasoning Necessary
papers.venue: arXiv 2026 · Korea University / AIGEN Sciences · first preprint 2026-09-06; v3 2026-09-11

zh.contribution: 让模型先把图像信息融入问题的内部表示，再通过共享层反复查看同一份视觉证据；回答时关闭其他视觉信息通路，并用替换状态等实验检验答案是否真的依赖这段计算。
zh.relevance: 补充主读之外的一个判断标准：内部有视觉表示，不等于答案使用了它。它把多模态推理的学习问题落实到 hidden state、attention 和 KV cache 的数据流，便于理解怎样设计有说服力的机制实验。
zh.reading: 值得精读 Figure 2、§3 和 §5.1–5.3，先画清初始化、循环更新、回答三个阶段，再对照 Table 2 看每一部分是否真正有用。重点是计算路径与干预证据，而非榜单名次。
zh.prerequisites: 知道模型逐步生成答案即可。正文解释隐状态、KV cache、共享层和 LoRA；无需先掌握因果推断公式，也不把隐藏向量等同于可读的思维步骤。
zh.caveat: 关闭的是绕过最终循环状态的视觉通路，不能据此宣称排除所有捷径或获得通用视觉推理。主要实验为单个训练种子，部分任务退步；不同循环深度分别训练，不构成无限增加推理计算就会提升的证据。依据 CC BY 4.0 的 v3 作解释性改写与评议。

sections.heading: 答对看图题，是否说明模型用了那段推理？
paragraphs: 先看一个自拟例子：图片里有红杯和白杯，问题是“红杯在白杯左边吗？”视觉语言模型会把图片与文字转成内部向量，再生成答案。有些方法额外加入几轮向量计算，希望模型在不写出文字推理的情况下重新检查空间关系。这通常称为 latent reasoning，即隐式推理；这里的隐状态是数值表示，不是一段藏起来的自然语言。

问题在于，回答模块可能仍能直接读取原来的图像信息。即使新增的计算毫无作用，模型也可能答对。论文先把若干已有方法的隐状态换成空白图像对应状态、另一道题的状态或噪声，同时保留原来的图文上下文。部分方法的准确率变化很小，例如 UniVLR 的三种替换都不超过 0.5 个百分点。这支持“该设置下不强依赖所替换内容”，还不能推出这些方法在任何任务上都没有作用。[§2 与 Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S2)

sections.heading: 先保留已经看懂的内容，再开始反复检查
paragraphs: CVRR 的第一步不是拿一个空白向量重新学看图，而是让预训练模型照常处理图片和问题。经过前面的层后，“红杯在白杯左边吗”这些问题位置的向量已经吸收了视觉信息。作者取出这些向量作为初始状态 h1，另外保存视觉位置的向量 v，供后面反复读取。h1 是一组随图片与问题变化的向量，每个位置仍对应问题中的文字片段（token）。

插入位置也不是随便选一层。作者在训练样本中找同一问题、不同图片且答案不同的配对，逐层交换视觉向量，观察答案偏好受到多大影响。他们希望找到问题表示已吸收足够视觉信息、视觉位置又仍有作用的位置。在主要的 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 实验中，边界选在第 20 层之后，第 21 层先以原有参数执行一次，形成 h1 和 v；测试基准不用于选择这个边界。[§3.1–3.2 与 Appendix H](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S3)

sections.heading: 循环期间继续看图，回答时只接收循环结果
paragraphs: 接下来，模型保留同一份 v，把上一次更新后的问题状态放回原来的位置，再执行同一个经过适配的第 21 层。共享参数不意味着每次做出相同结果，因为输入的问题状态已经改变。默认 T=4 包含一次原生初始化和三次更新；每次把旧状态与新计算结果各取一半，得到下一状态。红杯例子可以帮助理解反复查看的目的，但论文没有把三次更新分别标注成“找杯子—识别颜色—比较位置”。

循环结束后，CVRR 才移除视觉位置和原来的图文 KV cache。KV cache 是 attention 为后续生成保存的 key/value 向量；即使删除显式图像 token，保留含图像信息的旧缓存仍可能留下另一条通路。因此，下方各层只使用由纯文字问题产生的缓存，上方回答模块接收最终状态 hT。视觉信息必须经过 hT 才能影响答案，但循环过程中一直可以读取 v。[§3.2–3.3 与 Algorithm 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S3)

sections.heading: 训练的是一个小适配器，对照也必须重新训练
paragraphs: 主模型参数保持冻结，只训练共享循环层上的 LoRA。LoRA 用少量可训练矩阵调整原层的计算；本实验约有 288 万可训练参数，占总参数的 0.0348%。训练目标很直接：提高正确答案各 token 的概率，即答案上的交叉熵损失。虽然训练数据名叫 Visual CoT，本文的方法并不要求模仿教师写出的逐步思维轨迹，也不为每个隐状态指定正确内容。

主要训练使用 Visual CoT 的 43.8 万条问答，四张 B200 180GB GPU、全局 batch 128、三个 epoch，即把训练数据学习三遍；报告的是随机种子 0 的一次训练。作者另外训练保留完整图文通路的普通监督微调对照，以及六种能适配相同无旁路接口的隐式推理方法。后者不是简单在已训练模型上删掉图像就评价，而是在共同数据和训练设置下重新训练，尽量保留各自原有机制与目标。[§4.1–4.2 与 Appendix B](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S4)

sections.heading: 主要结果是保住能力，同时让路径确实必要
paragraphs: 先与原模型比较，才能避免把受限制对照的低分当作全面领先。CVRR 在 V* 上为 81.2%，原模型为 79.6%；在 MMVP 的配对准确率上为 52.7%，原模型为 47.3%。V* 只有 191 道高分辨率看图题；MMVP 有 150 对相似图片、共 300 个问题，配对准确率要求一对里的两题都答对。BLINK 总准确率仅从 55.0% 到 55.2%，MME-RealWorld-Lite 则从 50.8% 降到 46.7%。

更切合论文主张的是：同样关闭其他视觉通路并重新训练后，六种对照在 V* 上最高为 39.8%，CVRR 仍有 81.2%。这表明不能只强制答案通过一个隐状态，还要把预训练形成的视觉能力带入这条路径。与普通监督微调相比，CVRR 在 V*、MMVP 和 BLINK 上相当或更好，但这些结果仍不足以说明这套接口适合所有视觉任务。[Table 1 与 §4.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S4)

sections.heading: 怎样证明循环不是把已有答案转交出去？
paragraphs: 即使 hT 是必经之路，也可能只是转交 h1 中已有的信息。Table 2 因此分别去掉组件并重新训练：保留初始状态和学习到的更新层，但不再读取 v，V* 从 81.2% 降到 69.1%，MMVP 配对准确率从 52.7% 降到 18.0%；继续读图却去掉学习到的适配，也分别降到 76.4% 和 32.7%。这两组对照支持反复读取和学习到的更新各有作用。
作者还把一张图的初始状态与另一张图的视觉证据配在一起。干净证据能够把错误初始状态拉向正确答案，错误证据也会把正确状态带偏；关闭问题读取视觉位置的连接后，这两种影响大幅减弱。这比仅展示 attention 热图更接近“新读到的证据改变了后续计算”的证据。

另一个对照始终保持问题相同，只把最终状态换成另一张图对应的状态。例如仍然问红杯位置，只交换两种摆放图片的内部结果。在论文的 MMVP 机制分析中，准确率从 73.3% 降到 26.7%。这里主要依据第一个选项 token 的受限读出，不能与 Table 1 的完整生成准确率混用；它排查的是“是否仅因问题表示被破坏才答错”，支持答案确实跟随状态中的视觉内容。[§5.1–5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S5)

sections.heading: 必要路径不等于所有捷径都消失
paragraphs: 这套接口排除了视觉信息绕过 hT 的路线，没有排除数据中的答案规律、语言先验或已经存在于 h1 中的简单识别结果。依赖某个向量，也不自动意味着进行了人类可解释的多步推理。论文的干预和消融把证据推进了一步，但没有检验所有可能的捷径，也没有证明模型获得了开放环境中的通用视觉能力。这里始终重复读取固定证据，不会自行拍一张新图或主动取得新观察。
Appendix I 在 Gemma 和 InternVL 等额外主干上也测试了接口，因此证据不只来自 Qwen；但每个主干都要重新找插入边界，状态替换的影响大小也不同。主要机制分析集中于选择题，训练为单种子，置信区间来自对测试样本重采样，不能代表换训练种子后的稳定性。

计算也不是免费增加的。单张 B200、32 个样本、三次计时且不计图像预处理时，T=4 的测得延迟为 1.146 秒，T=1 为 1.044 秒。不同 T≥2 配置分别训练，T=1 则没有可训练循环适配器；更深配置的准确率也不单调上升。因此这组实验不能解释为同一模型在部署时多循环几次就一定更强。[§6 与 Appendices B、D、I](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S6)

sections.heading: 精读路线：把三段数据流画清楚
paragraphs: 建议先看 Figure 2，分别画出普通图文初始化、共享层更新、最终回答，标明每阶段可以读取哪些向量和缓存。再看 Table 2，问“如果删去这一部分并重新训练，能力是否还能保留”；最后读 Figure 4 的同问题状态交换，理解为什么需要控制问题本身不变。读懂这三处，比先记住所有指标更能迁移到其他隐式推理研究。

本文依据 Suhyeong Park、Junha Jung、Jaewoo Kang（Korea University / AIGEN Sciences）的 [v3 原文](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3)作解释性改写与评议：2026 年 9 月 6 日首发，9 月 11 日修订，按 2026 年预印本介绍。原文采用 [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)。红杯与白杯是本文自拟教学例子，用来说明数据流，不代表作者已经逐步解释了每个内部向量的语义；本文未重新训练或复现实验。

en.contribution: Starts from an image-conditioned question representation, repeatedly re-reads fixed visual evidence through a shared layer, then removes alternative visual routes before answering. State-replacement interventions test whether predictions actually depend on that computation.
en.relevance: Adds a criterion beyond the main paper: a representation containing visual information need not be used by the answer. It connects multimodal learning to hidden-state, attention, and KV-cache data flow, making the design of mechanistic experiments concrete.
en.reading: Read Figure 2, Section 3, and Sections 5.1–5.3 closely. First separate initialization, recurrent updating, and answer decoding; then use Table 2 to test the contribution of each component. Focus on computational paths and interventions rather than leaderboard rank.
en.prerequisites: Only autoregressive answer generation is assumed. The notes explain hidden states, KV caches, shared layers, and LoRA without requiring causal-inference equations or equating hidden vectors with readable reasoning steps.
en.caveat: The interface removes visual routes around the final recurrent state, not every possible shortcut or limitation in visual reasoning. Main experiments use one training seed and some tasks regress. Different recurrent depths are trained separately, so the results do not establish unlimited inference-time scaling. These notes adapt and discuss the CC BY 4.0 v3.

sections.heading: Does solving a visual question mean the proposed reasoning was used?
paragraphs: Consider our teaching example: an image contains a red cup and a white cup, and the question asks whether the red cup is to the left of the white cup. A vision-language model converts the image and question into internal vectors before answering. Some methods add several rounds of vector computation so that the model can reconsider spatial relations without writing a textual reasoning trace. This is called latent reasoning. The hidden state is a numerical representation, not a concealed natural-language paragraph.

The answer decoder may still read the original visual information directly. It could answer correctly even if the added computation contributes nothing. The paper first replaces existing methods’ proposed latent states with blank-image states, states from different examples, or noise while retaining the original multimodal context. Some methods change little: UniVLR moves by no more than 0.5 percentage point across the three interventions. This supports weak dependence on the replaced content in that setting, not the conclusion that those methods are useless on every task. [Section 2 and Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S2)

sections.heading: Preserve what the pretrained model already saw before revisiting it
paragraphs: CVRR does not begin with an empty vector and relearn vision. It first lets the pretrained model process the image and question normally. After the lower layers, vectors at the question positions already incorporate visual information. The method extracts these vectors as the initial state h1 and separately retains visual-position vectors v for repeated access. Here h1 is a collection of vectors conditioned on both image and question, with positions still corresponding to pieces of question text, or tokens.

The insertion point is selected rather than arbitrary. Using training pairs with the same question but different images and answers, the authors swap visual activations at successive layers and measure the change in answer preference. They seek a region where question representations already carry visual competence while visual positions still influence the answer. For the main Qwen2.5-VL-7B experiments, the boundary follows layer 20. Layer 21 then runs once with its native parameters to form h1 and v. Evaluation benchmarks are not used to select this boundary. [Sections 3.1–3.2 and Appendix H](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S3)

sections.heading: Keep reading the image during recurrence, then answer through its result
paragraphs: The model retains the same v, puts the latest question state back into its original positions, and executes the same adapted layer 21 again. Sharing parameters does not produce identical outputs because the question state changes. The default T=4 consists of one native initialization and three updates. Each update averages the previous state and the newly computed state. The cup example explains why revisiting evidence could help, but the paper does not label these updates as finding cups, identifying colors, and comparing positions.

Only after recurrence does CVRR remove visual rows and the original multimodal KV cache. A KV cache stores attention keys and values for subsequent generation; deleting explicit image tokens while retaining image-conditioned caches could leave another route. Lower layers therefore use caches produced from the text-only question, while the upper answer decoder receives the final state hT. Image-conditioned information must pass through hT to affect the answer, although recurrence can read v throughout its computation. [Sections 3.2–3.3 and Algorithm 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S3)

sections.heading: Train a small adapter, and retrain the relevant controls
paragraphs: The backbone remains frozen. Only LoRA parameters on the shared recurrent layer are trained. LoRA introduces small trainable matrices that modify the original computation; this experiment trains approximately 2.88 million parameters, or 0.0348% of the total. The objective is answer-token cross-entropy: increase the probability of correct answer tokens. Although the dataset is named Visual CoT, CVRR does not require imitating teacher reasoning trajectories or specifying a correct target for each latent state.

Main training uses 438,000 Visual CoT question–answer pairs, four B200 180GB GPUs, a global batch size of 128, and three epochs, or three passes over the training data. Results come from one training run with seed 0. The authors also train an ordinary supervised-fine-tuning control retaining the full multimodal path and six latent reasoners compatible with the same no-bypass interface. The latter are retrained using common data and training settings while preserving their mechanisms and objectives; this is not simply deleting images from already-trained models and evaluating the damage. [Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix B](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S4)

sections.heading: The central result is preserved competence with a required path
paragraphs: Start with the original backbone comparison rather than interpreting weak restricted baselines as universal superiority. CVRR scores 81.2% on V*, versus 79.6% for the backbone, and 52.7% MMVP pair accuracy, versus 47.3%. V* contains only 191 high-resolution visual questions. MMVP contains 300 questions over 150 similar-image pairs; pair accuracy requires both questions in a pair to be correct. BLINK overall accuracy moves only from 55.0% to 55.2%, while MME-RealWorld-Lite drops from 50.8% to 46.7%.

The comparison closer to the paper’s claim is that, after removing alternative visual routes and retraining, the six compatible baselines reach at most 39.8% on V*, while CVRR retains 81.2%. Requiring answers to pass through a latent state is therefore insufficient by itself; pretrained visual competence must enter that path. CVRR matches or exceeds ordinary supervised fine-tuning on V*, MMVP, and BLINK, but these results do not establish that the interface suits every visual task. [Table 1 and Section 4.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S4)

sections.heading: How do we know recurrence is not merely forwarding an existing answer?
paragraphs: Even a required hT could simply forward information already in h1. Table 2 therefore removes components and retrains. Keeping native initialization and the learned transition but removing further access to v reduces V* from 81.2% to 69.1% and MMVP pair accuracy from 52.7% to 18.0%. Retaining visual access but removing the learned adaptation yields 76.4% and 32.7%. These comparisons support contributions from both persistent evidence access and learned updates.

The authors also cross the initial state from one image with visual evidence from its paired alternative. Clean evidence can pull an incorrect initial state toward the correct answer, and incorrect evidence can pull a correct state away. Blocking question-to-visual connections largely removes both effects. This supplies stronger evidence that newly accessed information changes subsequent computation than attention visualizations alone.

Another intervention keeps the question fixed and replaces the final state with one obtained from the alternative image. In our example, the question about cup positions stays the same while the internal result from another arrangement is substituted. The paper’s MMVP mechanistic analysis drops from 73.3% to 26.7%. This analysis primarily uses restricted first-option-token readout, so it must not be mixed with Table 1’s full-generation accuracy. It tests whether disrupted question content alone explains the failure and supports dependence on image-conditioned content. [Sections 5.1–5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S5)

sections.heading: A required path does not eliminate every shortcut
paragraphs: The interface removes visual routes around hT. It does not eliminate answer regularities in the data, language priors, or simple recognition results already present in h1. Depending on a vector also does not automatically establish human-interpretable multistep reasoning. The interventions and ablations strengthen the evidence, but they do not test every possible shortcut or demonstrate general visual competence in open environments. The method repeatedly reads fixed evidence rather than taking a new image or acquiring a new observation.

Appendix I also tests Gemma and InternVL backbones, so the evidence is not exclusive to Qwen. However, the boundary is localized separately for each backbone, and sensitivity to state replacement varies. Main mechanistic analyses focus on multiple-choice settings. Training uses a single seed; confidence intervals come from resampling evaluation examples and do not measure variation across training runs.

Additional computation is not free. On one B200 over 32 examples, with three timing runs and image preprocessing excluded, measured latency is 1.146 seconds for T=4 and 1.044 seconds for T=1. Configurations with T≥2 are independently trained, whereas T=1 has no trainable recurrent adapter. Accuracy is also nonmonotonic across larger depths. This is not evidence that a deployed checkpoint becomes reliably stronger just by running extra iterations. [Section 6 and Appendices B, D, and I](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3#S6)

sections.heading: Reading route: draw the three stages and their available information
paragraphs: Begin with Figure 2 and draw normal multimodal initialization, shared-layer updating, and final answer decoding separately. Mark which vectors and caches each stage can access. Then inspect Table 2 and ask whether competence survives after removing a component and retraining. Finally, read Figure 4’s same-question state replacement to understand why the question itself must remain controlled. These three checks transfer to other latent-reasoning studies more readily than memorizing every score.

These notes adapt and discuss [v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06746v3) by Suhyeong Park, Junha Jung, and Jaewoo Kang of Korea University / AIGEN Sciences, first posted September 6, 2026 and revised September 11, as a 2026 preprint. The source is licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The red-and-white-cup example is our teaching construction for explaining data flow, not a claim that the authors decoded the semantics of each intermediate vector. We have not retrained or reproduced the experiments.

papers.title: Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
papers.venue: arXiv 2026 · CityU / Zhejiang / Peking / Nankai / Huawei · v1 2026-10-08

zh.contribution: 把视觉压缩改成持续管理证据：保留整张图的原始缓存，用小摘要维持整体信息，再随推理进展选择需要重新参与计算的细节。
zh.relevance: 适合思考多模态 rollout 的完整成本：视觉 token 少了是否真的更快，还取决于回答长度、首次响应、缓存存储和动态取用开销。
zh.reading: 值得精读 §3.1–3.3 的缓存与调度过程，再结合 §4.4 和附录 C 检查成本口径；它提供的是一种可训练的视觉证据访问机制。
zh.prerequisites: 知道模型逐个生成 token 即可；正文解释 KV 缓存、粗细两级视觉信息和路由决策，不要求先掌握状态空间模型公式。
zh.caveat: 只验证了一个冻结的 Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct；保留完整视觉缓存会增加峰值显存，首 token 也可能更晚。主要加速来自特定长输出评测，不能直接推出线上请求时延或其他解码设置的收益。

sections.heading: 1. 做到一半，才发现需要再看图上的小字
paragraphs: 想象一道教学题：图里有一个直角三角形，两条直角边标着 3 和 4，要求面积。模型先确认直角位置，再读两条边的数字，最后计算 3×4÷2。算乘法时不必反复看整张图，但如果一开始删掉了数字 4，后面再长的文字推理也补不回这条证据。
ViMoD 研究的就是这种变化：生成回答的不同阶段，需要看的图像区域可能不同。一次性选好并永久保留一小组视觉 token，未必能满足后面的需要。作者提出保存可再取用的细节，推理走到哪里，再决定让哪些细节参与计算。[§1、图 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 2. 完整细节留着，但每一步只读取一部分
paragraphs: 模型首先完整处理图片和题目，得到 KV 缓存：注意力计算以后可以复用的键和值。Fine KV 指原始视觉 token 在各层的这些缓存；Coarse KV 是把若干 Fine 条目汇总后的较小缓存。Coarse 始终参与后续计算，Fine 则按需加入。没被选中的 Fine 仍在存储中，因此重新读取无需从有损摘要里还原像素。[§3.1、算法 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

用一个计数例子理解预算：原有 90 个 Fine token，9:1 配置约产生 10 个 Coarse token。20% 目标意味着生成期间平均有约 18 个视觉条目参与计算，其中已经包含这 10 个摘要。它通过调节选择阈值校准平均用量，不保证每一步都恰好 18 个，更不表示只保存了原来 20% 的缓存。[附录 C.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 3. DART 学习怎样分组，避免小字和空白被同样处理
paragraphs: DART 负责构造摘要和分组。它从规则网格起步，学习每组应该包含多少原始 token，以及哪些 token 应该归到同一组；组的边界可以跨过初始网格。组数固定，全部原始 token 仍各自属于某一组。这样，空白区域可以汇总得粗一些，文字或直角标记附近可以分得更细。[§3.2、图 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)
每组保存一条 Coarse 摘要，以及回到原始 Fine 成员的索引。各层的键按学习到的权重汇总，值先经过一个小编码模块再汇总。需要细节时取回整组的原始 KV，而非把摘要放大；因此分组同时决定压缩效果和每次取回细节的成本，组里也可能夹带暂时用不到的内容。[§3.2、式 4–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 4. TRACE 根据已经写出的推理，决定接下来读哪里
paragraphs: TRACE 每生成 16 个 token 做一次选择。它读取隐藏状态，即模型对当前文字的内部表示，用一个小型状态空间模块持续保存不同时间跨度的历史摘要，再预测接下来需要哪些视觉组。可以把它理解成记录“刚才确认了直角，现在准备读边长”的内部状态；推理时只能利用已经发生的信息，不能偷看后文。[§3.3、附录 B 表 7](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)
它还判断继续保留当前组，还是换成新提议的组。更新可以增加、移除或清空细节；清空后仍有 Coarse 摘要可用。每层注意力一起读取 Coarse、当前 Fine 和文字历史，这个组合叫 Joint-KV。所谓按需回看，是切换哪些缓存参与计算，不是重新裁图后调用一次视觉编码器。[§3.3、附录 A.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 5. 模型怎么学会这些选择
paragraphs: 主模型 Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct 的参数始终冻结。先用 57,420 条经过任务检查的回答训练 DART，让压缩后的预测接近完整视觉输入下的预测。随后固定 DART，用 Qwen3.8-27B 为 80,000 个样例标出各段推理需要的图像框，训练 TRACE 选组和更新。这里只训练附加模块，参数合计约为主模型的 0.0546%；这个比例不包含标注教师。[§3.4、附录 B](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)
最后从上述样例中筛出 4,800 题，每题生成 16 条回答，用最终是否答对继续训练 TRACE；在同题的正确回答之间，再鼓励较少使用 Fine。训练同时保留教师对下一段证据的指导：教师看到图、题和学生已写出的前缀，看不到参考答案或学生未来文本。额外开销奖励并不保证准确率或用量满足硬约束。[附录 A.3、B.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 6. 80.33 这个分数，具体说明什么
paragraphs: 在八个推理基准、20% 目标预算和 9:1 配置下，ViMoD 的平均归一化得分为 80.33；一次性压缩方法中最强的 DivPrune 为 57.78。计算方式是每项分数先除以同设置下未压缩模型的分数，再乘 100 后取平均，因此它不是 80.33% 正确率。使用同一 DART 缓存、改成 DSTP 注意力变化规则来取证据的对照为 72.96，更有助于比较访问策略。[表 1、§4.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

所有方法都用逐步选最高概率 token 的贪心解码，presence_penalty 为 0。主表 MMMU-Pro 最多生成 4,096 个 token，未压缩基线得分 30.92%；作者指出技术报告为 53.2%，但没有隔离解码设置、重复和截断各自的影响。因此这些比较支持同一实验协议内的改善，不能直接对照外部榜单。[附录 C.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 7. 整轮更快，代价是启动更重、显存更多
paragraphs: 效率实验另用 MMMU-Pro、单张 H200、批大小 8、最多生成 8,192 个 token。40% 目标预算下，ViMoD 完成整轮评测的耗时比 FastV、VisionZip、DivPrune 少 15.2%–20.4%。这是整轮墙钟时间，不是平均请求延迟或服务时限保证。这些对照虽然每秒生成更多 token，却生成了比未压缩模型多 15.9%–29.9% 的文字，抵消了单步节省。[§4.4、附录 C.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

该实验未压缩模型 94.4% 的时间花在逐 token 生成上，足够长的回答摊薄了初始化成本。ViMoD 保留完整预处理并构造摘要，在 20%–50% 预算下，平均首 token 时间比一次性压缩对照更长。推理峰值 GPU 内存也由 Full 的 38.40 GiB 增至 42.67 GiB；这是总峰值，不是 KV 单项。少参与注意力和少占显存是两回事。[§4.4、附录 C.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 8. 值得带走的问题与阅读路线
paragraphs: 先看图 4 和算法 1，把“存着哪些证据”和“此刻读哪些证据”分清，再看表 1、图 6 和附录 C 的预算、时间口径。短回答、持续需要大范围图像细节、漏选组或更新太晚，都可能削弱收益；跨主模型和其他解码设置尚未验证。对系统工作的启发是联合记录答案质量、输出长度、首 token、整轮耗时与峰值内存。[§5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

本文依据 Yicheng Xue、Han Wu、Jufeng Yang、Minjing Dong、Xinghao Chen、Hanting Chen、Jianyuan Guo 于 2026 年 10 月 8 日发布的 v1 作解释性改写；团队涉及香港城市大学、浙江大学、北京大学、南开大学和华为。原文采用 [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)。三角形与 90-token 算例为本文构造，未复现实验或核验当前代码。[原论文与版本记录](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060v1)

en.contribution: Turns visual compression into ongoing evidence management: retain the complete original visual cache, preserve an always-active compact summary, and select details to participate in computation as reasoning evolves.
en.relevance: Useful for accounting for multimodal rollout costs: fewer active visual tokens translate into faster execution only in conjunction with response length, first-token latency, cache storage, and dynamic-access overhead.
en.reading: Read the cache and routing process in §3.1–3.3, then examine the accounting in §4.4 and Appendix C. The contribution is a trainable mechanism for accessing visual evidence.
en.prerequisites: Knowing that a model generates tokens sequentially is sufficient. The note explains KV caches, coarse and fine visual representations, and routing decisions without requiring state-space-model equations.
en.caveat: Only one frozen Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct backbone is evaluated. Keeping the full visual cache increases peak memory, and the first token can arrive later. Speed gains come from a particular long-output evaluation and do not establish online request latency gains or robustness to other decoding settings.

sections.heading: 1. Halfway through reasoning, a small label matters again
paragraphs: Consider a teaching example: a diagram contains a right triangle with perpendicular sides labeled 3 and 4, and asks for its area. The model first identifies the right angle, then reads the corresponding side labels, and finally computes 3×4÷2. It need not inspect the entire image repeatedly while multiplying. But if compression discarded the label 4 at the start, a longer textual explanation cannot recover that missing evidence.

ViMoD studies this changing demand: different stages of a response may need different image regions. Selecting a small, permanently fixed set of visual tokens once may fail to support later steps. The authors retain recoverable details and decide which ones should participate in computation as reasoning progresses. [§1 and Figures 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 2. Store the details, but read only part of them at each step
paragraphs: The model first fully processes the image and question to obtain KV caches: keys and values that subsequent attention computations can reuse. Fine KV denotes these original visual-token caches at each layer; Coarse KV is a smaller cache obtained by aggregating Fine entries. Coarse entries remain active, while selected Fine entries join them on demand. Unselected Fine entries remain stored, so recall does not require reconstructing pixels from a lossy summary. [§3.1 and Algorithm 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

A counting example clarifies the budget. With 90 original Fine tokens, the 9:1 configuration produces approximately ten Coarse tokens. A 20% target means about 18 active visual entries on average during generation, already including those ten summaries. A selection-threshold offset calibrates average usage. It does not impose exactly 18 entries at every step, and does not mean that only 20% of the original cache is stored. [Appendix C.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 3. DART learns groups that treat small labels differently from blank areas
paragraphs: DART constructs the summaries and groups. Starting from a regular grid, it learns both how many original tokens each group should contain and which tokens belong together; membership can cross the initial grid boundaries. The number of groups stays fixed, and every original token still belongs to one group. This allows coarser aggregation in blank areas and finer groups around text or a right-angle marker. [§3.2 and Figure 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

Each group provides a Coarse summary and an index back to its original Fine members. Layer-wise keys are pooled with learned weights, while values pass through a small encoder before pooling. Recall retrieves the group's original KV rather than enlarging its summary. Grouping therefore determines both compression quality and recall cost; a recalled group can also contain details that are not currently useful. [§3.2, Equations 4–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 4. TRACE uses the reasoning so far to decide where to look next
paragraphs: TRACE makes a routing decision every 16 generated tokens. It reads available hidden states—the backbone's internal representations of the current text—maintains summaries of history at different timescales through a small state-space module, and predicts the visual groups needed next. Intuitively, its internal state can track something like “the right angle has been established; next comes reading the side lengths.” At inference it uses only information already available, not future text. [§3.3 and Appendix B, Table 7](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

It also decides whether to retain the current groups or replace them with the proposed set. An update can add, remove, or clear details; Coarse summaries remain accessible even when the Fine set is empty. Attention at each layer jointly reads Coarse entries, active Fine entries, and text history, a combination called Joint-KV. Looking back means changing which cached entries participate in attention, rather than cropping the image and invoking the vision encoder again. [§3.3 and Appendix A.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 5. How these decisions are learned
paragraphs: The Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct backbone stays frozen. DART is first trained on 57,420 task-verified response trajectories to make predictions under compression resemble predictions with full visual context. DART is then frozen, and Qwen3.8-27B annotates the evidence boxes needed for reasoning segments in 80,000 examples, supervising TRACE's group selection and update decisions. Only auxiliary modules are trained, totaling approximately 0.0546% of the backbone's parameters; this count excludes the annotation teacher. [§3.4 and Appendix B](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

Finally, 4,800 questions are selected from that supervised set, with 16 responses generated per question. Final-answer correctness trains TRACE further, while lower Fine occupancy is rewarded among correct responses to the same question. Teacher guidance on upcoming evidence remains part of training: the teacher sees the image, question, and generated student prefix, but neither the reference answer nor future student text. The additional cost feedback does not impose a hard accuracy or usage constraint. [Appendices A.3 and B.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 6. What the score of 80.33 actually means
paragraphs: Across eight reasoning benchmarks at a 20% target budget with 9:1 memory, ViMoD's mean normalized score is 80.33, versus 57.78 for DivPrune, the strongest evaluated one-shot method. Each benchmark score is divided by the corresponding uncompressed model's score under the same settings and multiplied by 100 before averaging. Thus 80.33 is not 80.33% answer accuracy. A control that applies DSTP's attention-change access rule to the same DART memory scores 72.96, providing a more targeted comparison of access policies. [Table 1 and §4.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

All methods use greedy decoding—choosing the highest-probability next token—with presence_penalty=0. The main MMMU-Pro table permits up to 4,096 generated tokens, and the uncompressed baseline scores 30.92%. The authors note a technical-report score of 53.2%, but do not isolate the effects of decoding settings, repetition, and truncation. These comparisons therefore support improvements within the shared experimental protocol, not direct comparisons with external leaderboards. [Appendix C.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 7. A faster complete run, with heavier startup and more memory
paragraphs: A separate efficiency experiment uses MMMU-Pro on one H200, batch size eight, and a maximum of 8,192 generated tokens. At a 40% target budget, ViMoD completes the evaluation run in 15.2–20.4% less time than FastV, VisionZip, and DivPrune. This is complete-run wall-clock time, not mean request latency or a service-level guarantee. Those baselines generate more tokens per second but produce 15.9–29.9% more tokens than the uncompressed model, offsetting per-step savings. [§4.4 and Appendix C.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

In this experiment, autoregressive decoding accounts for 94.4% of the uncompressed model's runtime, allowing long outputs to amortize initialization. ViMoD preserves full prefill and builds Coarse memory; at 20–50% target budgets, its mean time to first token is higher than that of the one-shot baselines. Peak GPU memory also rises from Full's 38.40 GiB to 42.67 GiB. These are total inference peaks, not KV-only measurements. Fewer entries participating in attention does not imply less memory occupied. [§4.4 and Appendix C.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)

sections.heading: 8. Questions to take away, and a reading route
paragraphs: Start with Figure 4 and Algorithm 1, distinguishing stored evidence from evidence currently being read. Then examine Table 1, Figure 6, and Appendix C's budget and timing definitions. Short answers, sustained demand for broad visual evidence, missed groups, or late updates can weaken the gains. Other backbones and decoding settings remain unverified. For systems work, the useful lesson is to measure answer quality, output length, first-token time, complete-run time, and peak memory together. [§5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12060v1)
